# Remote Video Monitoring Cost: A California Business Owner’s 2026 Pricing Guide
## Remote Video Monitoring Cost: 2026 Industry Pricing Ranges
### Per-Camera Pricing
Most providers structure remote video monitoring pricing on a per-camera, per-month basis:

| Tier | Monthly Cost Per Camera | What’s Included |
|-|-|-|
| Basic (alarm response) | $30–$75 | Alarm-triggered review, incident reporting |
| Standard | $50–$150 | Scheduled live checks, audio deterrence capability |
| AI-enhanced | $100–$200+ | AI motion filtering, reduced false alarms, verified response |
| Continuous live | $200–$400+ | Human operators watching specified hours continuously |

### Per-Site Monthly Cost by Business Size
| Business Size | Camera Count | Monthly Remote Monitoring Cost |
|-|-|-|
| Small (retail, office, small warehouse) | 4–8 cameras | $200–$1,200 |
| Mid-size (distribution, larger retail, industrial) | 10–20 cameras | $500–$3,000 |
| Large (campus, logistics, multi-building) | 20–50 cameras | $1,500–$6,000 |

### Hourly Pricing (Activity-Based)
- **Low-activity sites** (overnight-only, minimal movement): $75–$100 per camera per month

## 5 Factors That Determine Your Monthly Remote Video Monitoring Bill
### 4. AI Integration and False Alarm Filtering
Pricing typically runs $100–$200 per camera per month for AI-verified monitoring.

### 5. Equipment vs. Monitoring-Only Pricing
Professional-grade camera installation runs $1,000 to $5,000 per camera depending on resolution, mounting complexity, and connectivity requirements.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### How much does remote video monitoring cost per camera per month?
Standard remote video monitoring costs $50 to $150 per camera per month for most commercial applications. Basic alarm-triggered monitoring starts around $30 per camera. AI-enhanced monitoring with verified human review runs $100 to $200 per camera. Continuous live monitoring — where an operator watches your cameras during specified hours — is typically priced at $8 to $10 per hour industry-wide. Guardian’s live video monitoring starts under $3 per hour of effective coverage, below the industry average for continuous monitoring.

### Does remote video monitoring work for small businesses?
Small businesses with four to eight cameras typically pay $200 to $1,200 per month for professional live monitoring — far less than any part-time guard arrangement and with coverage during hours that would otherwise be unmonitored.

# Cost of Live Video Monitoring Explained
For example, remote video monitoring services often cost $30 to $150 per month per camera, or around $65/month per camera for simpler setups.

## What Is Live Video Monitoring and Why Does the Cost Vary?
According to industry providers, the average cost for remote video monitoring services typically ranges from $100 to $500 per month, depending on the number of cameras, site risk level, and features included.

## Average Monthly and Yearly Cost of Live Video Monitoring
### Basic Monitoring Packages
**Cost:** $30–$60/month

### Mid-Tier Monitoring Packages
**Cost:** $60–$150/month

### Advanced Enterprise Packages
**Cost:** $200–$500+/month

## Additional Costs Homeowners and Businesses Should Expect
### Cloud Storage and Video Retention
A basic plan with 7- to 30-day retention can be as little as $2.99 per camera per month, while high-resolution video kept for 90 days or more can reach $20–$25 per camera per month.

## Comparing Live Video Monitoring Costs to Alternatives
### Live Monitoring vs Security Guard Costs
- Remote video monitoring, even with multiple cameras and AI, typically costs $100 to $500/month, depending on the scale and features.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### How much does live video monitoring cost per month?
Residential systems usually cost **$30–$80/month** for a few cameras and basic video. Small businesses pay **$100–$250/month** for more cameras, 24/7 monitoring, and alert verification.
